name: Flow Physics Facility
use: Boundary-layer wind tunnel for turbulence research
builtText: c. 2010 (described as UNH's newest building in UNH Magazine, Winter 2011)

facts.text: At 300 ft long and 20 ft wide it is described as the world's largest scientific-quality boundary-layer wind tunnel.
Two 400-hp fans each move 250,000 cfm, pulling air through garage-style doors at about 28 mph (UNH Magazine says up to 30 mph).
On Waterworks Road; features a 10-inch poured concrete floor, windows for external laser measurement, a turntable and floor drag plates.
A $3 million facility funded by NSF EPSCoR, the Office of Naval Research and UNH.
UNH Magazine called it architecturally bland and geographically isolated, with no students or faculty housed in it.

ceps.title: Flow Physics Facility
ceps.publisher: UNH College of Engineering and Physical Sciences

verdict: A 300-ft shed housing the world's largest scientific boundary-layer wind tunnel: unique inside, bland and isolated outside.
notes: notunh has no name for it (inventory notunh null); it may not be on the map. No licensed photo; reference shows a dark tall interior hall with two big fans and a polished floor.
